subject: Immediate action required: Glyph experiencing throttling due to quota window mismatch
messages:
From: Erin Cho <erin.cho@glyphtech.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Support Team <support@glyphtech.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production throttling and latency spike — urgent

Rachel —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and tail latency around 08:45 Pacific this morning. Impacting our ingestion pipeline (bulk embeddings). Requests that previously succeeded are now getting rejected after 2–3 retries. Our SREs collected traces and there are repeated 429s with a note "quota_exceeded: burst_disabled" in the response body.

This is high priority for us — we have a nightly job that must complete by 02:00 UTC and it's failing. Can you confirm if there was any change to our quota/burst configuration? Our account id is G-1432.

Attached: support_log_20271003.txt (sampling of request IDs and timestamps).

—Erin
Erin Cho
Platform Reliability Lead, Glyph Technologies
erin.cho@glyphtech.com

From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
To: Erin Cho <erin.cho@glyphtech.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throttling and latency spike — urgent

Thanks Erin — I'm escalating immediately and looping in support and eng. We see the ticket HB-45873 in our side as well.

Short answer: we haven't intentionally changed Glyph's committed capacity, but I'm putting the right people on it to identify whether a policy rollout or config drift caused this. Expect an update within 60 minutes.

Actions I'm taking now:
- Sean: please gather recent quota/burst policy changes and confirm whether the burst allowance for G-1432 is enabled.
- Markus: please check the routing policy and per-customer quota windows for the last three deploys.
- Marissa: FYI; Glyph is flagged for NRR and is high-touch — they need prompt resolution.

I will keep the thread updated and coordinate any temporary mitigations (short-term burst enable, capacity bump).

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0143

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, Erin Cho <erin.cho@glyphtech.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throttling and latency spike — urgent

Erin / Rachel —

I pulled the logs and aligned them with the attached support_log_20271003.txt. Key observations:
- 429s start at 08:44:12 PT and correlate with bursts of concurrent short-lived embedding requests.
- The control plane shows quota checks failing against a per-minute window while the routing policy enforces a per-second smoothing rule.
- In short, the customer profile had an override that set the quota window to 60s but the new routing policy expects a 1s sliding window for burst credits. The migration script that rolls policy compatibility missed converting the "burst_enabled" flag for accounts with legacy overrides.

Temporary mitigation applied at 09:58: we re-enabled burst_credits for G-1432 and applied a conservative per-second allowance. I can confirm immediate drop in 429s on our side.

Attaching: support_log_20271003.txt (annotated).

Next steps (technical):
1) Markus to propose permanent fix for the migration script + a validation job.
2) Run a backfill to reconcile quota windows for all legacy override accounts.
3) Postmortem with timeline and proposed credits/compensation.

Sean Gallagher
Technical Support Manager, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throttling and latency spike — urgent

Team —

Root cause summary: during last week's policy consolidation (deploy v2027.10.01) we introduced a new default quota window normalization layer. The migration we ran intentionally left "legacy_override" accounts untouched, but the conversion step that maps legacy "burst_allowance" boolean -> new "burst_profile" object failed to run for ~2.1k accounts due to an indexing bug. Glyph's account had a legacy override (set during onboarding) and therefore never got the new burst_profile; the system treated them as having burst_disabled by default.

Evidence: see attached burst_policy_config.yaml (excerpt) showing Glyph's policy snapshot before/after. I validated the change we applied at 09:58 (re-enabled burst_profile.low) and verified through synthetic traffic that their job passed.

Proposed permanent fix (timeline):
- Hotfix migration script to be deployed within 6 hours (today).
- Validation job to run overnight for all legacy_override accounts (~4–6 hour run).
- Add a preflight check to deploy pipeline to catch missing conversions in future policy consolidations.

I'll open PR with the migration and include unit tests + a one-off reconciliation job. I recommend we also proactively reconcile accounts in the next 48 hours even if they haven't yet reported impact.

Markus Klein
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Attachments: burst_policy_config.yaml (snippet)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: execs@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Glyph production impact — proposal for credits and communication

Team / Execs —

Summary: Glyph (G-1432) experienced throttling for ~74 minutes due to migration script not converting legacy burst flags. Impact: delayed nightly ingestion job, elevated 429s and tail latency. Root cause identified and temporary mitigation applied by Support. Permanent fix and reconciliation scheduled.

Asking for approvals:
- Approve a one-time service credit equal to 10% of October hosted tier invoice (proposal attached: proposal-temporary-credits.pdf).
- Approve customer notification language (I drafted an email below).

Draft customer note (short):
Hi Erin — we’re very sorry for the disruption. We identified a migration issue that caused your account to lose burst credits during a recent policy consolidation. We have re-enabled burst credits, deployed a hotfix to prevent recurrence, and are running a reconciliation. We've also proposed a one-time credit as a gesture of goodwill. We expect to share a postmortem within 48 hours.

Please approve the credit and the customer note so Rachel can send ASAP.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
To: Erin Cho <erin.cho@glyphtech.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throttling and latency spike — urgent

Erin —

Thank you for your patience. Quick update:
- We re-enabled your burst credits at 09:58 PT which resolved the 429s.
- Markus has a hotfix migration script being prepared and we'll run a reconciliation for legacy_override accounts overnight.
- Marissa has proposed a one-time credit; pending exec approval, we'll apply it to your October invoice.

Next steps for you:
1) Can you confirm the nightly job ran to completion after 10:00 PT? If you still see artifacts, send the IDs and we'll triage.
2) We're planning a short postmortem with timeline (within 48 hours) and will share the plan to prevent recurrence.

Apologies again — we understand this was disruptive and are treating it as high priority.

Best,
Rachel
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
